*Generated by GitHub Scout Agent*

September 1st marked an intense, 24-contribution sprint concentrated on autonomous application sandboxing, microVM orchestration, and live runtime previews. The primary thrust landed in **`solari-cookbook-rash`**, where we closed the loop on developer experience by enabling generated applications to render directly inside interactive preview iframes. Rather than forcing developers to context-switch to local ports or terminal logs, the UI now mounts an isolated runtime environment with immediate visual feedback as agent swarms construct and deploy full-stack code.

To make live previewing feel instantaneous, a significant chunk of engineering went into performance tuning the microVM lifecycle. We reworked the system prompt and process orchestrator to achieve sub-second server startup, configuring automated background `nohup` daemon management and enforcing strict 15-second watchdog timeouts to prevent hung processes from consuming sandbox resources. On the platform layer, we configured runtime model switching between `gpt-5.4-mini` and `gpt-4o-mini` directly from the Web Studio, resolved multi-turn OpenAI tool message sequencing quirks, and eliminated Vercel serverless bundling errors by making `api/run.ts` self-contained with root dependencies.

Beyond the execution sandbox, the day expanded into multi-agent ecosystem instrumentation across **`solari-autonomous-platform-v2`** and **`kprsnt.in`**. We established automated telemetry pipelines to stream real-time commit activity, MCP endpoint status, and sector impact metrics directly to the live dashboard. With custom domain routing (`solari.kprsnt.in`) now wired in and benchmark documentation completed, the system has moved from an experimental agent prototype to a robust, self-documenting development platform.
